newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai CP group, Siemens sign China wafer plant pact.
newsitem.headline: Thai CP group, Siemens sign China wafer plant pact.

text.p: Thai conglomerate Charoen Pokphand (CP) Group signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Germany's Siemens AG to supply technology for a proposed semiconductor plant in China, executives said on Thursday

"We have signed an MOU with Siemens and we are discussing three possibilities. We are starting out with Siemens as a technology partner in the wafer fab(rication)," said Vallobh Vimolvanich, President of Telecom Holding, a high-tech investment arm of CP and its subsidiary TelecomAsia.

He told Reuters that further possibilities being discussed included a possible equity stake, or other investment roles, for Siemens in the US1.2 billion project, as well as a possible downstream development of wafer packaging.
In November CP Group signed an MOU with the Shanghai Municipal Authority and the Ministry of Electronic Industries to build the wafer fabrication plant in Puodong.
He cautioned that CP was not yet guaranteed to receive central government approval for the project.
CP currently has a 31 percent stake in the project and the Chinese partners 69 percent.
The factory will produce logic, clock and processor wafers but not computer memory DRAM wafer, Vallobh said.
Whatever the outcome, CP was interested in building a second US$ 1.2 billion plant either in Hong Kong or Thailand and expected to announce an investment decision by the middle of 1997, Vallobh said.
He said CP had made informal approches to Thailand's Board of Investment asking for more than existing maximum privileges to locate there.
Chinese authorities had indicated to CP executives that incentives to set up in Hong Kong following the China's takeover from Britain this July would be considerable, Vallobh said.
CP Group is one of the largest current investors in China and is one of Thailand's largest companies with interests ranging from animal feeds to satellites.
